exposure: passive or quitting smoking before or in the first trimester
lowest or highest quartiles of birth weight
outcome: poor breastfeeding success (exclusive breastfeeding < 4 months and total breastfeeding < 6 months)
successful breastfeeding (exclusive breastfeeding >= 4 months or breastfeeding with formula >= 6 months)
cohort: The study included 2,521 women from the Kuopio Birth Cohort study who answered online questionnaires 1 year after giving birth.
finding: Poor breastfeeding success was significantly associated with several factors, most notably maternal fear of childbirth, smoking during pregnancy, twin pregnancy, maternal obesity, and birth during earlier periods (2013-2016).
mod_finding: Birth by nonelective cesarean was related to poor breastfeeding success, but the strong association between mother's fear of childbirth and poor breastfeeding success remained even after controlling for mode of birth.
birth_weight: Lowest or highest quartiles of birth weight.
